title: Dynamical Systems Seminar – Tommaso Cornelis Rosati
desc:
Speaker : Tommaso Cornelis Rosati

Title : Lyapunov exponents for linear cocycles driven by stochastic Navier-Stokes

Abstract : We provide the first convergence result for finite time Lyapunov exponents of Passive Scalar Advection and Linearized Stochastic Navier-Stokes (two linear cocycles driven by the stochastic Navier-Stokes equations). The proof is based on establishing unique ergodicity for a Markov process with values in an infinite-dimensional projective space. Uniqueness of the invariant measures requires an extension of asymptotic coupling tools, and proving a generic non-collinearity for passive scalar advection. Joint work with Sam Punshon-Smith.

title: Control and Optimisation seminar – Jacco Thyssen (York)
desc:
Title

When No One Learns, Everyone Can Coordinate: Public Signals in Dynamic Adverse Selection

Abstract

We consider a model with dynamic adverse selection and public news. We show that embedding simple return and buy-back options in spot sale contracts implements the full-information first-best allocation. Even if the public signal never fully reveals the seller’s private information, it remains critical for implementation. The signal serves as a coordination device that enables screening of informed agents and achieves separation at the initial stage. Strikingly, the signal’s correlation with the private information is essential for implementation, even though uninformed agents learn nothing from the signal. We apply the model to a buyer–seller setting, rationalizing the pervasive…

title: SPC Seminar – Space – Dr. Mariana Jeunon Barros (QMUL)
desc:
Abstract: In this work we investigate a series of six 3He-rich events that were observed by Solar Orbiter on 10/29/2022-10/30/2022. We find possible candidates for the solar sources of such events and present a Differential Emission Measure (DEM) analysis to further characterize the plasma conditions that led to their eruption. By comparing the plasma properties of the six events, we can compare the distinct characteristics of each of the sources that could have led to more 3He enhancement.

This study demonstrates that there is a temperature range (1.86-4.1MK) which is associated with 3He enhancement. Our results show that 3He enrichment depends not only on temperature, but also on the thermal structure of the plasma, particularly the width and peak temperature of individual thermal…
